<p class="page-deck">An ongoing comparative programme examining how authority, finance, organisational capability, infrastructure provision, participation, coordination, sequencing and maintenance combine to deliver urban climate action.</p>

**Work type:** Ongoing research programme<br>
**Status:** Ongoing<br>
**Relationship to the lab:** Current CCLL work — Research developed before the lab was established and published after Andrew joined Simon Fraser University; foundational to the lab's current delivery programme.<br>
**Primary theme:** [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html)

## How this work contributes to climate learning

**Primary theme:** [Modes of Climate Delivery](/research/modes-of-climate-delivery.html)

**Secondary connections:** [Geographies of Climate Learning](/research/geographies-of-climate-learning.html)

**Decision or problem:** How cities can make climate action operable and durable through configurations of authority, finance and coordination.

**Delivery conditions:** The programme studies configurations rather than treating a delivery mode as an intervention, technology or sector label.

**Evidence status:** Owner-approved current programme connected to a verified peer-reviewed framework paper.

**Claim boundaries:** No delivery configuration is presented as universally suitable or effective, and no unpublished IPCC material is used.

**Next learning question:** Which delivery conditions recur across places, and which remain context dependent?

### Research facets

**Geographies:** canada, global<br>
**Climate domains:** mitigation, adaptation<br>
**Sectors:** cross-sectoral, urban-infrastructure<br>
**Methods:** comparative-case-study, institutional-analysis, policy-analysis

## Research questions

- Which configurations of authority, finance, capability and participation make urban climate action possible and durable?
- How do delivery arrangements vary across city types, sectors and institutional settings?
